description: One evaluation of the circumstances one vessel is in, under the COLREGS, with three readings. signals: every complete, lawful set of navigation lights self may show, from her fact record (propulsion, activity, position, length, and the other facts in colregs data/facts.json): the applied entries; exempted (relieved by a rel:exempts entry) and overridden (displaced by a superior obligation's rel:overrides) entries, each with the entry that did it; and lawful_displays: {count, relation, options}. relation is "none", "exactly_one" or "any_one_of". A fact record describes a situation, not a fitted vessel: colregs data/facts.json has no equipment fact, so nothing in the input can settle a choice the Rules leave to how the vessel is fitted or what the skipper elects, such as Rule 25(b), the combined masthead lantern a sailing vessel under 20 m may carry, against Rule 25(c), the all-round red over green she may add. When lawful_displays.count is greater than 1, every option is equally lawful, the correct report is all of them, and reporting any one as "the" display for this vessel is wrong. Displays are listed in the order to consider the rules in, most specific concession first, and the first is the one a vessel of that description usually shows. Each option numbers itself "n of count", names the choice entries that distinguish it (chosen) and lists its lights with their own modality, so "shall" and "may" lights in one display are never merged. optional_additions are lawful extras (relation any_subset_of) that do not multiply the display set. Every id carries its paragraph cite, and cited_paragraphs holds the verbatim text of every cited paragraph. appraisal: what Part B requires of self on her own, then against each other vessel (kind of encounter, risk of collision, each vessel's role). indicated: per other vessel, what her observed lights, shapes and sounds say she could be. appraisal and indicated are passed through from colregs-engine as returned, without the cite resolution signals has. Compliance over time is not read yet. Not for navigation. Coverage: COLREGS Part C lights only, international (high seas) text only, lights at night only (no day shapes, no sound signals, no Part B steering rules), evaluated against pre-release colregs data (0.x), whose content is still being checked. Every entry id and paragraph cite in a response is verbatim from the colregs data package; nothing is paraphrased. This tool surface is a 0.0.x preview and will change without notice.

conditions.description: Keys namespaced `env:*` per colregs-engine. The water: narrow channel, traffic lane.

others.description: The other vessels, each as self knows her.

act.description: Keys namespaced `act:*` per colregs-engine. What she is doing or intending now.

bearing_deg.description: Her bearing relative to self's heading.

fact.description: What she is, as asserted by the caller.

fact:activity.description: Cites: activity:fishing: 3(d); activity:trawling: 26(b); activity:nuc: 3(f); activity:ram: 3(g); activity:ram_underwater: 27(d); activity:cbd: 3(h); activity:mine: 27(f); activity:pilot: 29(a); activity:diving: 27(e); activity:towing: 24(a); activity:pushing: 24(b); activity:being_towed: 24(e). 'ram_underwater' is a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver that is dredging or engaged in underwater operations (27(d)); it is a refinement of 'ram', not a peer of it, and predicates written for 'ram' also read it.

fact:confined_to_channel.description: Cite 9(b). A vessel which can safely navigate only within the narrow channel or fairway -- 9(b)'s and 9(d)'s protected vessel, read of whichever vessel it is asked of rather than assumed from `pair:env:narrow_channel`. Closes Q-34's 9(b)/9(d) half: a consumer sets this from the vessel's draft and the channel, the same judgement `pair:env:narrow_channel` already asks of a chart or an ENC.

fact:following_traffic_lane.description: Cite 10(i). Following a traffic lane of a scheme adopted by the Organization -- 10(i)'s and 10(j)'s protected vessel, read of whichever vessel it is asked of rather than assumed from `pair:env:traffic_lane`. Closes Q-34's 10(i)/10(j) half.

fact:full_display_impracticable.description: Cite 27(e). 27(e)'s gate: the diving vessel's size makes it impracticable to exhibit all the lights and shapes of 27(d). The Convention leaves that judgement to the vessel and no source reduces it to a length (IMO text and Annex I, 33 CFR 83.27, the UK, Canadian and NZ variants, Cockcroft & Lameijer), so this package asks rather than inventing a threshold, as for 'very large vessel' (Q-42). Absent reads as false: the full 27(d) display.

fact:length_m.description: Cite 3(j). Unit: m. Length overall. COLREGS thresholds are 7, 12, 20, 50 and 100 m.

fact:making_way.description: Refines fact:position=position:underway. Undefined in the Rules; it means moving through the water. Underway but not making way is free drifting. Only the 26/27-family predicates read it (26(b)(iii), 26(c)(iii), 27(a)(iii), 27(b)(iii)); Rules 23 and 25 gate on 'underway' alone, so a power-driven vessel drifting in neutral still shows full running lights.

fact:manned.description: Cite 35(e). 35(e)'s condition on the towed vessel's own signal: the last vessel of a tow sounds it only if she is manned.

fact:max_speed_kn.description: Cite 23(d)(ii). Unit: kn. Read only by 23(d)(ii). No SignalK path publishes it; design.maxSpeed does not exist in the schema. Kept because the rule has it.

fact:motorsailing.description: Refines fact:propulsion=propulsion:power. Proceeding under sail when also being propelled by machinery. Rule 3(c) makes her a power-driven vessel, so the lights are Rule 23's; 25(e)'s cone is the only signal that reads this.

fact:near_channel.description: Cite 30(e). At anchor in or near a narrow channel, fairway, or where other vessels normally navigate.

fact:nearing_obscured_bend.description: Cite 34(e). Nearing a bend, or an area of a channel or fairway where other vessels may be obscured by an intervening obstruction. A place fact in the family of `fact:near_channel`, read of one vessel and set by the helm from the chart.

fact:non_displacement.description: Cite 23(b). Air-cushion vessel operating in non-displacement mode.

fact:on_mooring_buoy.description: Refines fact:position=position:moored. Made fast to a mooring buoy rather than to the shore. Rule 3(i) makes both 'moored', and the Convention prescribes no lights for either. Only a jurisdiction that deems a buoy-moored vessel to be at anchor reads it -- US Inland, 33 CFR 90.5 -- so under intl it selects nothing.

fact:partly_submerged.description: Cite 24(g). The vessel or object being towed is inconspicuous and partly submerged, or a combination of such vessels or objects. True selects 24(g) in place of 24(e); absent leaves her on 24(e).

fact:position.description: Cites: position:underway: 3(i). Rule 3(i): underway means not at anchor, not made fast to the shore, not aground.

fact:propulsion.description: Cites: propulsion:power: 3(b); propulsion:sail: 3(c); propulsion:oars: 25(d)(ii). A vessel under sail with propelling machinery in use is 'power' (Rule 3(c)); the 25(e) day shape is the only trace motorsailing leaves at night.

fact:seaplane.description: Cite 3(e). The vessel is a seaplane, an aircraft designed to manoeuvre on the water; her lights are the power-driven vessel's, and Rule 31 is what reads this.

fact:tow_display_impracticable.description: Cite 24(h). From any sufficient cause it is impracticable for the vessel or object being towed to exhibit the 24(e) or 24(g) lights or shapes. The Convention leaves the cause to the vessel, so this package asks rather than deriving it, as for fact:full_display_impracticable.

fact:tow_length_m.description: Cite 24(a)(i). Unit: m. From the stern of the towing vessel to the after end of the tow.

fact:tow_restricts_deviation.description: Cite 27(c). The towing operation severely restricts the towing vessel and her tow in their ability to deviate from their course. Rule 27(c) makes such a pair restricted in her ability to manoeuvre; `activity:towing` alone does not, because most tows are not. Read only by the fact:rule18_class decode table, which is where Q-32's missing 27(c) case lives.

fact:wig.description: Cite 23(c). The vessel is a wing-in-ground craft. Doesn't by itself mean 23(c) applies -- see wig_near_surface.

fact:wig_near_surface.description: Cite 23(c). Taking off, landing, or in flight near the surface. 23(c) is scoped to this phase, not to being a WIG craft generally.

geo.description: Keys namespaced `geo:*` per colregs-engine. Pairwise geometry about her (CPA, TCPA, risk_of_collision).

hist.description: Keys namespaced `hist:*` per colregs-engine. What has already been true of her and latches.

kin.description: Keys namespaced `kin:*` per colregs-engine. Her absolute kinematic state.

known.description: How self knows of her: Rule 11 in sight, Rule 19(d) by radar alone, Rule 19(e) heard.

observed.description: What self sees or hears of her: light, shape and sound ids, never what she exhibits.

range_nm.description: Her range from self, nautical miles.

self.description: The vessel whose obligations and signals are read.

act.description: Keys namespaced `act:*` per colregs-engine. What she is doing or intending now, stated, never derived.

fact.description: What this vessel is and is doing.
